data.narrative:
First Light Fusion is a Series C–stage nuclear energy company founded by Nicholas Hawker and Yiannis Ventikos, having raised over $100M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of 11 peers across nuclear energy: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables in the nuclear sector—only one adjacent-stage peer was identified against a minimum threshold of three. Consequently, the valuation relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $100M+ total raised as a proxy base. This method yields an implied valuation of $170M. The 1.7x multiplier reflects observed venture patterns for frontier-tech companies advancing from Series C into later rounds, absent company-specific margin or revenue data that would support revenue or earnings multiples.

The triangulation, constrained to a single applicable method, supports a median valuation of $170M, with a range of $144.5M to $195.5M reflecting reasonable variance around the stage-progression estimate. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable-company multiples (given sparse peer coverage at First Light's exact stage and valuation tier) and lack of visibility into unit economics or capital-intensity trajectories specific to the company's inertial confinement fusion approach.
